assignments.evidence: Fixed filiation formula 'NAME sutufako NAME girisfako' in every funerary text: the mother's slot, paired with giris 'begotten by (father)'.
Benediction 'kikrira gun/suse/zura gukhira' (given, like zohu 'beer'); counted in temple offering lists beside oxen, sheep and fields.
Benediction 'wu gun pafora' (poured, like sezi 'water'); counted as a liquid in offering lists ('wu 40 yune wolomu').
Counted livestock: 'folofudu 568 ma nedu 165 sapezo' (oxen and cows taken), 'ne 6 miyu 20' in offerings, 'nedu 5' in dedications.
Royal annals: first of the counted people taken ('yowidu N fokladu N pasodu N hizadu sapezo') and the ones killed ('yowidu wakizo').
Always second in the people count after yowi, before the optional paso, and never killed.
Optional third people category in the count ('pasodu 85'), present in only some lists, after men and women.
Closes every people count with no numeral, 'hizadu sapezo': men, women and children taken as captives.
'duwodu/fefukradu/kunalirdu resdozo' right after 'PLACEbi seyozo' (went to PLACE) and before taking captives: a conquest verb.
'fupurne/sune yumu dapukzo': temple in the object case for a god, followed by 'lurufo N gukhizo' (gave gold).
Dedications: listed goods (cows, gold, silver, beer, oxen) then 'yubi dultuzo', i.e. given to the temple.
Royal epithet 'monharzas RNAME fupurne/sune dozezo' after temple building: the king loved, or was beloved of, the god; the only verb left.
The only title that takes god names as its complement ('haltuto sune', 'fupurne', 'yane': 135 times); the other titles take only places.
Most frequent kin term in descriptive filiation (about 2x any other), yet absent from the 'NAME KINfako NAME' family labels.
Kin term; the most common in short family labels 'NAME dabonfako NAME' (16, ahead of pizu 'son' 12), as a wife label would be.
Kin term in the same slots as zitomu with the same frequencies; brother versus sister is a guess.
Kin term in the same slots as galu with the same frequencies; sister versus brother is a guess.
Default benediction adjective (half of all 'X ADJ gukhira/pafora'), alternating with suse 'good' and zura.
Second benediction adjective on water, milk, bread and beer, next to good (cf. 'good and pure' offerings); never said of the deceased.
'pirafako' is a predicate of the deceased, never in the same text as 'susefako' (is good), and never in benedictions.
Only in the closing wish 'wepakne togulra' (may [the god] protect [him] in X); life fits no other slot.
'wutibi dultuzo' alternates with 'yubi dultuzo' (offered to the temple): a building that receives offerings.
Seized in the annals ('kunalirdu resdozo') and also a generic place after titles ('gemoyun kunalirne NAME'), like yune 'in the temple'.
Seized object in the annals ('duwodu resdozo'), never a place after a title; land versus boat is a guess.
Seized object in the annals ('fefukradu resdozo'), never a place after a title; boat versus land is a guess.
Official title with place complements and no gods; the most frequent 'NAME TITLE' label (16); envoy, general and scribe are not separable.
Official title with place complements and no gods; its dedications are mostly oxen and sheep (booty?); a weak guess.
Official title with place complements and no gods; the remaining official title; a guess.
